subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU data residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>
To: Sven Müller <sven.mueller@finbank.de>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.in>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.in>
Date: 2027-06-12T09:15:00Z
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU data residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Sven —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we’re aligned: 

Call highlights:
- FinBank will run customer-facing chat agents and transaction classification in EU regions (GDPR sensitive).
- Peak throughput estimate: ~120k tokens/min; bursty daytime traffic across CET zone.
- Primary constraint: EU data residency and vendor-managed key controls; some regulatory customers may require customer-managed KMS or on-prem options.

Deployment options we discussed (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to deploy, multi-region routing available (we can pin EU-only routing), Redwood retains control plane. Good for quick POC or non-regulated data.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools in EU region (SLA, tenant isolation) with optional KMS integration and limited inbound VPC peering.
- Private VPC / On-prem: private control plane + on-prem inference for customers who need full network isolation and customer-managed keys. This is the strongest fit for regulated workloads but requires longer lead time.

Region/residency notes relevant to FinBank:
- We can serve EU-only inference from our Frankfurt and Dublin regions.
- For Hosted API, cross-region fallback is possible (e.g., to us-west) but only with explicit agreement — by default we can pin EU region to prevent cross-border processing.
- Private deployments can be fully air-gapped or provisioned in your VPC in AWS eu-central-1; some customers have combined Private control plane (in EU) with on-prem or VPC inference nodes.

Attachments I’m sharing: SOC2 summary, short slide on deployment options, and a draft mutual action plan (MAP) with timeline.

Suggested next steps:
1) Could you confirm whether FinBank requires customer-managed KMS for all EU workloads or only for the high-risk product verticals?
2) If yes to (1), we should schedule a technical call with our Solutions Engineer (cc’d: Aditya) to scope the KMS and network setup.
3) If the goal is to go-live in Q4, we recommend locking dedicated capacity or starting Private onboarding discussions this quarter.

I’m available Wed/Thu afternoon CET for a 30-min technical follow-up.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.in | +1 (415) 555-0123

- deployment_options_slide.pdf (1-pager)

From: Sven Müller <sven.mueller@finbank.de>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.in>
Cc: Lena Fischer <lena.fischer@finbank.de>
Date: 2027-06-12T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & EU data residency (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A few clarifying points from our side: 

1) KMS: For core payment flows and any PII we will require customer-managed KMS in EU. For lower-risk tooling (internal summaries), we can consider vendor-managed keys as long as data doesn't leave the EU.
2) Cross-region fallback: We cannot allow automatic failover to non-EU regions for EU-customer data. If Redwood needs to failover, it must be to another EU region and only after we approve the change.
3) Private vs Dedicated: Our security team prefers Dedicated in EU for production (isolation + SLA) and Private for the highest-risk product that deals with direct account linking. Cost/ops will influence the decision — can you add a short comparison table (security controls, lead time, ops complexity, estimated monthly cost range)?

We’d like to schedule the technical call next Thursday 2027-06-17 at 10:00 CET if that works for your team. CC'ing Lena who will coordinate internal attendees.

Best,
Sven
Head of Platform Security, FinBank
Sven.Mueller@finbank.de

Thanks Sven — that’s helpful and aligns with what we expected. Quick answers and next steps: 

- KMS: We can support customer-managed KMS for all EU production workloads. Aditya will bring our Security Engineer to the technical session to cover key wrapping, rotation, and audit evidence.
- Cross-region failover: We will configure routing policies to restrict EU data to EU regions only and require an explicit change request (with approval flow) for any non-EU failover. We’ll document this in the MAP as a required approval gate.
- Comparison table: I’ve asked Neha to pull a succinct security/ops/cost comparison and add it to the MAP. Expect an updated MAP and the cost ranges by EOD Monday.

Technical call: 2027-06-17 10:00 CET works for us. Aditya and Neha are booked for that slot. I’ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda: 1) KMS & networking, 2) deployment topology (Dedicated vs Private), 3) timeline & MAP milestones.

If you can send any security questionnaire items ahead of the call, our Security team will prep answers.

Cheers,
